recipes.name: Spinach and Tortellini Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 (10 ounce) package frozen chopped spinach, thawed and drained
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rolling boil; stir in tortellini and return to a boil. Cook uncovered, until tortellini float to the top and the filling is hot, about 3 minutes. Rinse under cold water; drain.
Combine tortellini, tomatoes, spinach, cheese, and olives; add enough salad dressing to coat. Toss; season with salt and black pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Spinach and Tortellini Salad
raw_recipe.description: This spinach and tortellini salad recipe tosses cheese tortellini with spinach, Parmesan cheese, cherry tomatoes, black olives, and Italian dressing.

review.reviewBody: Fantastic! I've made this a few times and it is always a big hit. I use baby spinach and I don't bother cooking it. I just toss it in. When the spinach is mixed in the salad, the dressing naturally wilts as if it were cooked. I would highly recommend doing it this way.

I make this salad a lot in the summer and I make it a main dish by adding shrimp. We don't like olives and tomatoes so I add diced onion and radishes, quartered. 8oz Italian dressing is way too much! I use 1/4-1/2c. dressing. Also I use fresh spinach and some fresh garlic too. Light easy summer meal with no need to heat up the kitchen!

This recipe gets 5 stars for versatility and easiness!! I used marinated artichoke hearts instead of olives and chopped baby spinach instead of frozen. Mixed the packet Italian dressing in the blender and poured over salad and let marinate overnight. It was the first thing to go at the Easter picnic!

Delicious. I'm trying to eat more veg, so I added in 1 chopped red bell pepper, a stalk of celery, and like others, just used fresh baby spinach as it wilts nicely in. I added some black olives and a full container of baby bocconcini and about 1/2 cup of parmesan cheese. I used Renee's Creamy Italian as the dressing. This will be a lovely lunch each day for my work week.

This is a version of one of the most well-received dishes I make for get-togethers. It's also extremely versatile. We have learned that we much prefer to add the dressing to the tortellini the night before (or at least several hours). Sometimes it requires a little more dressing on the final mix (because it soaks up), but it really boosts the blending of the flavors. I also (like others) use fresh baby spinach. It's also great with cucumber. I like to add cooked chicken pre-marinated in the dressing or this amazing NY Italian Sausage from a local meat shop. I usually use Ken's Lite Northern Italian or Ken's Lite Caesar. We do much prefer shredded Parmesan to the grated, but that's just personal taste. I also add pepper, garlic powder, and onion powder to taste. I love the cherry or grape tomatoes in it - the color is beautiful and they add a lot to the taste. I do leave them whole, partly because they look better to me and are still easy to eat, and partly because my husband doesn't care for them and they are easy to pick out that way. I ALWAYS double this recipe, even for small groups, because there is never enough. With the exception of the spinach, it all holds really well as leftovers, so if I leave some at home for later, I don't put the spinach in it then. All in all, this is a fantastic dish - easy, versatile, pretty, and a little different.

This is a very easy and versatile recipe that can be modified to suit your taste. I used a 19 oz. bag of frozen cheese tortellini but kept other measurements about the same. I added some chopped mozzarella. I mixed together everything except the spinach and tossed it with about 1/2 bottle Italian dressing. I let that marinate in tupperware in the fridge during the day. About an hour before serving I mixed with fresh baby spinach leaves and added a bit more dressing. The fresh spinach will wilt down a bit as it sits before serving. If you don't have a large group you can use just what you need and save some of the tortellini mix in the tupperware to make more the next day (or days later) with more fresh spinach.

My daughter made this (after I cooked and drained the pasta) and we all enjoyed it. She taste-tested a few different dressings and decided to use Newman's Own Greek dressing. She also used fresh baby spinach versus frozen. Using tortellini made for a heartier pasta salad, which was perfect, as this was our main course.

WOW! absolutely fantastic. My husband said Olive Garden any one? 
i used fresh spinach and put chopped up zucchini in it.
I think a splash of lemon, a little onion and garnish with a salad pepper would be awesome.
i mixed in parmesan and sprinkled it on top. thanks for sharing the recipe!!

This was so good. My husband loved it. As others, I put fresh baby spinach uncooked and it was perfect. I added sliced red onion and small pieces of pepperoni. I used some Kraft roasted red pepper italian dressing with a little olive oil. Quick and easy recipe.
Very easy and goes well with many things. Had it with grilled burgers. Doubled the amount of pasta and omitted the cheese. Made Good Seasons dressing with balsamic for the dressing. Delicious.
Made a few simple adjustments; used fresh, organic baby spinach (uncooked), added salami. Used Annie's Tuscany Italian dressing. It was a huge hit!
This was one of the easiest and fresh tasting salads we have had in awhile. I made our Italian dressing and added fresh spinach instead of frozen. Very Very good. This is a summer time keeper!
Excellent easy recipe! Loved by the whole family!!! Will try fresh spinach next time, should have read the recipes before hand! Will make this again!!
I used fresh spinach because I had it on hand. We liked this recipe very much. I would definitely try it again!
I made this salad as a part of a luncheon and everyone enjoyed it.
I absolutely love this and it's so easy to make.
I, too used fresh baby spinach, added crumbled blued cheese instead of Parmesan, & used Green Goddess dressing I get at Trader Joe’s. Delicious,,
- When you need a potluck dish in a hurry! Use chopped fresh spinach - the dressing will wilt it. I used Kraft's new pesto/olive oil Italian dressing - great flavour!

Very colorful, easy, and tasty salad. The only change I made this time around was my use of fresh spinach, to me cooked is too slimy unless is the creamed variety. I would recommend starting with less dressing and then adjusting it to taste. I tend to go much lighter on my salad dressings than many people do
I double it . I use shredded Parmesan cheese. make this a day ahead and toss with a little more dressing before serving
